title: invocation gap detector and SLO proximity dashboard
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add invocation-gap metric and dashboard; introduce synthetic gap-replay test harness; new alert rule for SLO proximity using gap-rate heuristic; roll out staged by tenant; no API breaking changes.
description: Motivation: We observed production incidents where inference output stalls (a pause between emitted token chunks) caused customer-facing latency spikes that weren't well represented in existing latency histograms. These 'invocation gaps' often correlate with kernel contention, KV-cache stall on large prompts, or transient network backpressure. This PR introduces an invocation-gap detector metric and a SLO-proximity dashboard to make these events visible and actionable. What this PR implements: 1) Telemetry: a new span attribute 'invocation.gap_ms' emitted by serving runtime when inter-token idle time exceeds a configurable threshold; a derived counter metric invocation_gap_count{reason,tenant,model,region}; a distribution metric invocation_gap_duration_ms{tenant,stage}. 2) Detector: a lightweight server-side detector that emits gap events into our telemetry pipeline with an enumerated reason taxonomy (kv_cache_miss, kernel_backpressure, grpc_retries, unknown). The detector is conservative by default (threshold 120ms) and configurable per route/tenant via feature flags. 3) Synthetic test harness: tests/synthetic_gap_replay.py - a replay generator that produces controlled gap patterns for e2e verification and CI gating. 4) Dashboard: dashboards/slo_proximity/gap_and_slo_proximity.json - an observability dashboard showing tenant-level SLO proximity, gap-rate heatmap by model, waterfall of gap reasons, and a scatter of gap-duration vs token-cost. 5) Alerting: alerts/gap_rate_slo_proximity.yaml - new alert rule that considers both gap_rate and current SLO burnrate to suppress noisy alerts; uses a Poisson-windowed baseline to avoid thrashing. 6) Backfill/rollout plan: The new metrics are backfilled where available over 7 days; rollout staged to internal tenant groups first, then to all production after 48h monitoring. Design notes: Detector lives in src/telemetry/gap_detector.go; it hooks into invocation loop with minimal critical path work (sample and emit only when threshold crossed). We attach sparse context tags to avoid cardinality explosion and use coarse-grained reason tags. The dashboard uses aggregated rollups (5m) to keep query costs low. CI/testing notes: Unit tests added for detector logic and reason classification; synthetic_gap_replay validates end-to-end ingestion and dashboard panels locally; initial CI showed a flaky test in replay harness (timing) which was fixed by switching to wall-clock tolerant assertions. Security and privacy: No customer PII emitted; tenant IDs are hashed when exported to public dashboards. Rollback: feature flag to disable emission per route; revert patch will remove all telemetry keys. Related work: builds on ENG-1132 (kv cache profiler) and ties to ENG-2461 SLO telemetry sprint. Checklist: - [x] Add metric emission and span attribute - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Add dashboard and alerting rules - [x] Add rollout plan and feature flag - [x] Update docs (observability runbook) Operational impact: Initial estimate of additional metrics write amplification is ~0.6% at baseline traffic with default threshold; added rollups keep long-term storage nominal. Monitoring: we will watch cost delta and refine reason taxonomy in a follow-up (ENG-2510).

review_thread: Ethan Ross: Nice end-to-end approach. Concern: how do we avoid exploding tag cardinality if reason is set per callsite? Please ensure reason taxonomy is constant and low-cardinality.
Maya Patel: Reason taxonomy is fixed to the 4 enums in gap_detector.go and is documented in the runbook. We attach callsite only in an internal-only debug tag behind a flag (not exported to metrics).
Priya Menon: CI initially failed on synthetic_gap_replay due to timing flakiness; tests looked racy. Suggest using clock-mocking or tolerances.
Maya Patel: Switched replay to wall-clock tolerant assertions and added retries in CI harness. Re-ran the job and it passed.
Carlos Ortega: Alerting rule looks good but could be noisy for low-volume tenants. Recommend a minimum-invocations guard (added as threshold 50 invocations per 5m) and documented how to opt-out.
Maya Patel: Added min-invocations guard and a feature-flagged opt-out per tenant; included in rollout steps. Approved after minor nit fixes.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge to main after approvals and green CI. Deploy gated by feature flag; rollout started to internal tenants on 2026-02-18 and promoted to full production after 48h of monitoring.
